page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 2 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 CPU model running at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and is optimized for EBS and network-intensive tasks. Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1514.0. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. The multi-core stress-ng score is 3043.47, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2757.0, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 57.94 GB/sec (average) but a lower write large block bandwidth of 20.86 GB/sec (weak).

Due to its 2-core dedicated ARM configuration and 4.0 GB of RAM, the c7gn.large is suited for lightweight compute-optimized workloads, network appliances, and basic web serving. It exhibits poor performance in heavy multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (17.68 GB/sec) and Passmark CPU encryption (274.06). It is also limited in LLM inference, achieving 57.57 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model. This instance represents a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-based development, CI/CD pipelines, and network-bound microservices that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage.
